messages.subject: Re: Warnings during compilation and unable to reuse fitted stan models in R
parts:
On Wednesday, August 31, 2016 at 5:05:13 AM UTC-4, Paul Viefers wrote:
Dear all

Starting today, I get some strange behavior in R using stan. In short, I can compile stan models and sample from them, but 
  • rstan pastes a series of warnings into the console (see below) - no clue what they mean, and
Those are just compiler warnings. Don't worry about them.
• I cannot use a fitted model so sample from it again (see below).
You can't just pass a stanfit object to the first argument of stan() like

> fit2 <- stan(fit, data=c("T",
+                          "y",
+                          "x"),
+              iter=500,
+              chains=1)
Error in path.expand(path) : invalid 'path' argument

The (now outdated) way to do this is to pass it to the argument named fit, like

fit2 <- stan(data = c("T", "y", "x", fit = fit, iter = 500, chains = 1)

but it shouldn't recompile if you just do

fit2 <- stan(model_code = code,, data = c("T", "y", "x"), iter = 500, chains = 1)

which is not to say that only running 1 chain is a good idea.

Ben
